llm.summary: This skill is a simple odds lookup helper that calls The Odds API, with no hidden persistence or local data access.

dimensions.detail: Network access to The Odds API and use of its API key are proportionate to fetching betting odds; no local files, profiles, sessions, or unrelated services are accessed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single Markdown skill file declaring curl, jq, and an ODDS_API_KEY credential; no installer, scripts, dependencies, or bundled executable code are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are narrow and visible: run curl against a specific odds endpoint and process the response with jq.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, scheduled tasks, memory writes, background agents, or tool modification behavior appears in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is World Cup 2026 odds aggregation, but the actual operational content only shows an outright-winner futures query through The Odds API; prediction-market and match-line claims are broader than the implemented instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable providing an Odds API key. Treat the current skill as an outright World Cup winner futures lookup, not a complete sportsbook-versus-prediction-market comparison tool, and avoid sharing logs or transcripts that include the full curl URL with your key.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified as a scope/quality mismatch: the artifact advertises prediction markets, Polymarket comparison, group-stage odds, and match lines, while only documenting one outright futures API call. This does not show hidden or harmful behavior.
[E1] expected: Verified that the sample command sends ODDS_API_KEY to the intended odds provider in the request URL. That is purpose-aligned but users should avoid exposing command lines or logs containing the key.
